summary: A companion app is assembled from documentation portals, model-as-code views, runtime traces, and decision browsers. The essential implementation feature is a generated, navigable view whose elements retain links to authoritative artifacts and freshness metadata.

items.text: Backstage TechDocs builds documentation from repository sources, commonly in CI, stores the generated site, and renders it inside the software catalog; this connects discoverable system pages to owned source repositories.

Structurizr uses a versionable DSL to create a C4 software-architecture model and multiple diagrams, documentation, and decision views from that shared model, supporting consistent layered navigation.

Docusaurus documentation versioning creates addressable snapshots while its static build preserves normal source-control review; a companion can label current and historical views rather than silently replacing them.

Log4brains renders repository-local architecture decision records as a searchable static site with a chronological decision log and Git-derived metadata, exposing rationale alongside other companion views.

Jaeger stores distributed traces and provides trace search and span visualizations; linking a companion's component view to live traces supplies runtime evidence rather than an architecture-only narrative.
